claims.claim: Eos links zinc-based long-duration storage manufacturing to grid reliability and renewable-integration needs, but current evidence shows manufacturing throughput improvement without proof that scale has crossed into positive unit economics.

The causal chain is storage demand -> Eos manufacturing capacity -> project delivery -> grid-duration capacity; the binding successor bottleneck is economic conversion of throughput into positive gross margin rather than demand alone.

risks.risk: Alternative storage chemistries and grid solutions can satisfy portions of the same reliability need if Eos cannot improve delivered economics.

unknowns.unknown: Sustained high-utilization unit economics for Line 2 are not established.

claims.claim: Rapid revenue and backlog growth do not yet falsify the financing/execution risk because Q2 gross margin remained deeply negative and FPUSA represented material revenue/backlog concentration.

The strongest present falsifier of an uncomplicated scale thesis is that faster production has not yet demonstrated positive unit economics; this is a risk clarification, not a present methodology blocker.

risks.risk: Customer/project concentration and negative gross margin can turn nominal scale into greater cash consumption if conversion economics lag.
Guidance-range tightening and manufacturing-consolidation evaluation indicate execution remains adaptive rather than settled.

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not quantify dilution or external-financing needs through the point of sustainable positive gross margin.
